item.title: Stochastic Optimization for Personalized Screening Policies in Chronic Diseases
item.description:
Overview A stochastic optimization approach to designing individualized breast cancer screening schedules based on patient-specific risk profiles.

Problem Motivation One-size-fits-all screening policies result in over-screening for low-risk individuals and delayed detection for high-risk individuals.

Methodology Formulated the screening problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) incorporating uncertain disease progression.

Key Findings The optimal policy derived from the POMDP significantly improved the quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) while reducing total screening costs.
